\section[aeger, aegra, aegrum]{aeger, aegra, aegrum — sick, ill}

\label{lesson:LA-C68-aeger}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Latin for medicine, then the Latin for an illness.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: aeger, aegra, aegrum}
\textbf{aeger, aegra, aegrum} — \textquotedblleft{}sick, ill\textquotedblright{}. The opposite of \textbf{sānus}.

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for sick, tired, hungry, thirsty.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{aeger}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{aeger}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} say \emph{aeger}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Latin for medicine, then the Latin for an illness, then say \emph{aeger} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does aeger, aegra, aegrum mean? (\textquotedblleft{}Sick, ill\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
